title: Indicators for characterising online hate speech and its automatic detection
benchmark_measurement: Detection of hate speech against religious (Jews, Muslims) and ethnic/social (Roma, immigrants) groups in Italian tweets, based on a novel classification scheme of seven hate indicators.
findings: The study found significant differences in the characteristics of hate speech across target groups. Tweets targeting Jews showed a very high percentage (>90%) of 'intention to harm' and 'will not redeem'. In contrast, tweets targeting Muslims had a comparatively low percentage (20%) of explicit 'hate expression'. Machine learning models were generally more effective at identifying tweets that incite hatred and violence, which are considered more dangerous, across all target groups including religious ones.
